theorems.title: The pole of the zeta function
theorems.statement: The series for ζ(s) on Re s > 1 extends meromorphically to the plane. At its only pole the expansion begins ζ(s) = 1/(s−1) + γ + O(s−1), where γ is Euler’s constant.
theorems.use: Taking the logarithmic derivative of this expansion specifies the two centering terms in the smoothed prime sum.
theorems.citation: T. M. Apostol, NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §25.2(i) and (ii), especially (25.2.4).

theorems.title: Euler product for a Dirichlet character
theorems.statement: If χ is a Dirichlet character and Re s > 1, then L(s,χ) is the absolutely convergent product over primes p of (1−χ(p)p⁻ˢ)⁻¹. A prime dividing the modulus contributes the factor 1.
theorems.use: Taking the logarithmic derivative turns each Euler factor into a sum over powers of its prime. That sum supplies the weights in the Mellin transform.
theorems.citation: T. M. Apostol, NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, (25.15.2).

theorems.title: Dirichlet nonvanishing at one
theorems.statement: For every nonprincipal Dirichlet character χ the continuation of L(s,χ) is holomorphic at 1 and L(1,χ) is nonzero.
theorems.use: This makes L′(1,χ)/L(1,χ) a finite centering constant. The principal character requires the separate pole calculation.
theorems.citation: T. M. Apostol, NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §25.15(i) and (25.15.9).

theorems.title: Removing Euler factors at a larger modulus
theorems.statement: If χ modulo q is induced by χ₀ of conductor d, then L(s,χ) equals L(s,χ₀) times the product of 1−χ₀(p)p⁻ˢ for p dividing q. The identity holds meromorphically.
theorems.use: At Re s > 0 every added factor is nonzero, so changing level preserves zeros there.
theorems.citation: T. M. Apostol, NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, (25.15.4).

theorems.title: Reflection for a primitive Dirichlet character
theorems.statement: For primitive χ of conductor q, put a=0 or 1 according as χ(−1)=1 or −1. The completed function Λ(s,χ)=(q/π)^((s+a)/2)Γ((s+a)/2)L(s,χ) satisfies Λ(s,χ)=εχΛ(1−s,χ̄), where |εχ|=1.
theorems.use: In the open critical strip the gamma factors are finite and nonzero. A zero on the left therefore gives a zero for the conjugate character on the right.
theorems.citation: T. M. Apostol, NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §25.15(i), primitive functional equation (25.15.5)–(25.15.6).

theorems.title: The boundary of the critical strip
theorems.statement: The only zeros of ζ outside 0 < Re s < 1 are the negative even integers. In particular there are no zeros on Re s = 1.
theorems.use: Once both open halves of the strip have been handled, this identifies the exceptions in the classical statement about all zeros.
theorems.citation: T. M. Apostol, NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §25.10(i).

theorems.title: Changing the order of integration
theorems.statement: On two σ-finite measure spaces a nonnegative measurable function has the same integral in either order, possibly infinite. For a complex measurable function, finiteness of the integral of its absolute value makes both iterated integrals exist almost everywhere and gives the same value. One may take the completed measures.
theorems.use: In the Mellin identity one variable has counting measure. In the theta integral a majorant must first control two noncompact variables.
theorems.citation: Terence Tao, An Introduction to Measure Theory, §1.7, Theorem 1.7.18 and Corollary 1.7.23.

theorems.title: Cauchy’s estimate for derivatives
theorems.statement: Suppose g is holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed disk of radius R about σ, with |g| ≤ M on the circle. For each k ≥ 0, |g⁽ᵏ⁾(σ)|/k! ≤ M/Rᵏ. This follows by bounding the integrand in Cauchy’s derivative formula and multiplying by the circumference.
theorems.use: Subtracting the principal part of an isolated pole gives such a g. The estimate quantifies the advantage of the pole when its distance from σ is smaller than R.
theorems.citation: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §1.9, Cauchy’s integral formula for derivatives, (1.9.31).

theorems.title: Uniqueness of analytic continuation
theorems.statement: Two holomorphic functions on a connected open set agree throughout it if they agree on a set having a limit point there. For meromorphic functions the same conclusion follows by removing their poles locally.
theorems.use: This carries an equality from the half-plane where an integral converges into the region where the continued coefficients are evaluated.
theorems.citation: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §1.10(ii), Analytic Continuation.

theorems.title: Legendre’s formula for a factorial
theorems.statement: For a prime p and integer n ≥ 0, the exponent of p in n! is ∑ⱼ≥₁ ⌊n/pʲ⌋. Each integer from 1 to n contributes once for each power of p that divides it.
theorems.use: This is the valuation gained when one passes from a Taylor coefficient to a derivative.
theorems.citation: Gennady Eremin, Legendre’s formula and p-adic analysis, §1, formula (1).

theorems.title: Orthogonality of finite characters
theorems.statement: On a finite abelian group the average of a character is 1 for the trivial character and 0 otherwise. Indeed, translating the sum by a group element multiplies it by the value of the character at that element.
theorems.use: Applying the identity to a subgroup retains exactly the characters trivial on that subgroup in the arithmetic balance. On a four-dimensional residue space the same identity turns the fibre equation into an additive-character sum.
theorems.citation: Keith Conrad, Characters of Finite Abelian Groups, Theorem 4.1 and Corollary 4.2.

theorems.title: Orbit–stabilizer counting
theorems.statement: When a finite group G acts on a set, the orbit of x is in bijection with the cosets of its stabilizer. In particular the orbit size divided by |G| equals 1/|Stab(x)|.
theorems.use: The same pairs can be counted by first fixing a lattice or by first fixing a marked subspace. The reciprocal stabilizer order is the weight in the second count.
theorems.citation: Keith Conrad, Group Actions, Theorem 3.16.

theorems.title: Product formula in a number field
theorems.statement: For nonzero a in a number field, multiply |a|ᵥ over all places, using the normalized absolute values, with the complex modulus squared at a complex place. The product equals 1.
theorems.use: The scalar and determinant in a rational similitude contribute cancelling local Jacobians over all places.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Theorem 7.15.

theorems.title: Local classification determines a global Hermitian space
theorems.statement: Let E/F be quadratic over number fields. Two nondegenerate Hermitian spaces over E of the same rank are isometric if their localizations are isometric everywhere. At nonsplit finite places the determinant modulo local norms distinguishes the two classes of a given positive rank. At real places becoming complex one uses the whole signature. For a global space the product of the local determinant signs is +1.
theorems.use: To represent a given nonzero length in a plane, compare it with a diagonal plane whose first vector has the prescribed length. An isometry carries that vector into the given plane. For a definite subspace this classification identifies the rational space after adjoining one determinant line. The product condition also rules out a single nontrivial inert determinant sign.
theorems.citation: Benedict H. Gross, Incoherent definite spaces and Shimura varieties, §3, especially Theorem 3.1.

theorems.title: Hasse’s norm theorem
theorems.statement: Let L/K be a cyclic extension of number fields. An element of K× that is a norm at every completion is the norm of an element of L×.
theorems.use: In the dyadic argument the extension is quadratic. A choice of real signs supplies the norm condition at infinity and the ideal calculation supplies it at the finite places.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, Chapter VIII, Theorem 3.1.

theorems.title: Kronecker’s criterion for a root of unity
theorems.statement: A nonzero algebraic integer whose conjugates all have absolute value at most 1 is a root of unity. Its powers have bounded degree and bounded coefficients in their monic minimal polynomials, so two powers coincide.
theorems.use: A quotient of conjugate generators is a unit. Checking its complex absolute values now restricts the ambiguity to roots of unity.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Proposition 5.5 and Corollary 5.6.

theorems.title: The logarithmic lattice of units
theorems.statement: In a number field with r real places and s complex places, the logarithms of the units form a full lattice of rank r+s−1 in the product-formula hyperplane. The kernel is the finite group of roots of unity.
theorems.use: The lattice gives a compact torus when integrating along the center. Its rank also determines how many independent unit directions a determinant can measure.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Theorem 5.9 and the preceding description of the logarithmic map.

theorems.title: The S-unit theorem
theorems.statement: Let S be a finite set of places of a number field containing all its infinite places. The elements with valuation zero outside S form a finitely generated group. Modulo roots of unity it is free abelian of rank |S|−1.
theorems.use: Allowing denominators at primes above ℓ adds one free direction for each such prime in the generator estimate.
theorems.citation: Paul Fili and Zachary Miner, A generalization of Dirichlet’s S-unit theorem, §1, statement of the S-unit theorem.

theorems.title: Hilbert’s Theorem 90
theorems.statement: In a cyclic field extension F/K generated by γ, an element v of norm one has the form z/γ(z) for some z in F×.
theorems.use: After two twisted-norm classes yield the same finite data, their ratio has norm one. Writing that ratio as a coboundary gives the descent used in the kernel count.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, Chapter II, Corollary 1.23.

theorems.title: Artin reciprocity and the existence of class fields
theorems.statement: Fix a modulus 𝔪. Let I be the fractional ideals prime to 𝔪, and P the principal ideals whose generators satisfy its congruences and real sign conditions. For every subgroup H with P ⊆ H ⊆ I there is a class field L/K whose Artin map induces I/H ≃ Gal(L/K). A prime outside 𝔪 maps to arithmetic Frobenius.
theorems.use: For the ordinary ideal class group this gives the Hilbert class field. Prime-ideal classes can therefore be prescribed by choosing Frobenius elements.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, Chapter V, Theorems 3.5 and 3.6.

theorems.title: Chebotarev’s density theorem
theorems.statement: For a finite Galois extension L/K and a conjugacy class C in its group G, the unramified primes of K with Frobenius in C have density |C|/|G|. Excluding finitely many primes preserves this density.
theorems.use: The argument chooses auxiliary primes with a prescribed action. Its extra conditions on residue degree are treated in the cited passages.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Theorem 8.31.

theorems.title: The Chinese remainder theorem
theorems.statement: For pairwise comaximal ideals I₁,…,Iₙ in a commutative ring R, reduction identifies R/(I₁⋯Iₙ) with the product of the R/Iⱼ. Thus each compatible list of independent residues is attained.
theorems.use: Coprime moduli let the prime selection impose several congruences at once. They also let an exponent act independently on different primary parts.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 10.15.4, tag 00DT.

theorems.title: Local Tate duality with finite coefficients
theorems.statement: For a finite extension K of ℚₚ, a finite continuous Galois module A and its dual Aᴰ=Hom(A,μ∞), cup product and the local invariant give perfect pairings between Hⁱ(K,A) and H²⁻ⁱ(K,Aᴰ), for 0 ≤ i ≤ 2.
theorems.use: In degree two the local group order becomes the order of a dual invariant group. This is one of the factors in the localization calculation.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems, second edition, Part I, §2, Corollary 2.3.

theorems.title: Poitou–Tate duality for localization
theorems.statement: Let A be a finite Galois module over a number field, unramified outside a finite set S containing the archimedean places and the places dividing |A|. Localization in degree two has cokernel dual to H⁰(K,Aᴰ). At real places the sequence uses modified local cohomology. Write Shaⁱ(A) for the kernel of localization in degree i. There is also a perfect pairing of Sha²(A) with Sha¹(Aᴰ).
theorems.use: For odd ℓ the archimedean corrections vanish for ℓ-primary coefficients. The cokernel gives the global invariant factor in the localization count. The kernel pairing gives equality of the orders of the two finite locally trivial groups in descent.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems, second edition, Part I, Theorem 4.10.

theorems.title: The Chowla–Selberg product over imaginary quadratic ideal classes
theorems.statement: For an imaginary quadratic field of fundamental discriminant D<0, put F(z)=√Im(z) |η(z)|², h=|Cl(K)|, and w=|μ(K)|, the number of roots of unity. Write χᴰ for the quadratic character of D. The product of F over the CM points of the ideal classes equals (4π√|D|)^(−h/2) times the product of Γ(a/|D|)^(wχᴰ(a)/4) for 1 ≤ a ≤ |D|.
theorems.use: Taking logarithms turns the product into a class mean. The period calculation specifies the additional scaling for lattices whose discriminant has been normalized to one.
theorems.citation: A. Barquero-Sanchez et al., Faltings heights of CM elliptic curves and special Gamma values, §3, (3.2), and Theorem 5.1 at conductor one.

theorems.title: Cauchy–Binet for a Gram determinant
theorems.statement: Let X be a complex m by r matrix, m ≥ r. The determinant of X*X is the sum of |det Xᵢ|² over all r-element sets of rows i, where Xᵢ is the corresponding square submatrix. This follows by applying the product formula for determinants of rectangular matrices to X* and X.
theorems.use: For a basis of a Gaussian plane in four dimensions the six two-row minors therefore measure its determinant. The first two values can be counted exactly. A second use expands a compressed Hermitian exponential as a probability-weighted sum over its eigenvalue subsets.
theorems.citation: Andrew Putman, The Cauchy–Binet formula, Theorem 0.1.

theorems.title: Siegel–Weil in the convergent unitary range
theorems.statement: In the unitary dual pair over a quadratic extension of number fields, let the Hermitian target have dimension b and Witt index w, and let the doubled source have split rank a. When b−w>a, the theta integral of the standard Schwartz test converges absolutely. For the associated section of the Siegel induced representation the Eisenstein series is regular at (b−a)/2 and its value equals that integral with the measures of the formula.
theorems.use: Here a<b, so a target of Witt index zero also lies in this range. Expressing the target integral with probability measure produces the explicit inverse volume in the chapter.
theorems.citation: Shunsuke Yamana, The Siegel–Weil formula for unitary groups, Pacific J. Math. 264 (2013), pp. 236–237, convergence criterion and Theorem 2 in the case m−r>n.

theorems.title: The Rallis inner product formula at first occurrence
theorems.statement: In the unitary case of the cited theorem let n<m≤2n, and let the target have Witt index r≤n. Suppose π is irreducible cuspidal and its theta lifts to the smaller indices in this tower vanish. The pairing of two theta lifts is [E:F] times the value at s=(m−n)/2 of the product L(s+1/2,π×χ)Z*(s), with χ the splitting character attached to the target space V and Z* the normalized doubling integral for the chosen vectors.
theorems.use: The factorization identifies the global L-value and the normalized local factors. The chapter supplies the formula for its own ranks and follows the measure and vector normalizations at each step of the chain.
theorems.citation: W. T. Gan, Y. Qiu and S. Takeda, The regularized Siegel–Weil formula (the second term identity) and the Rallis inner product formula, §11.6, (11.3), and Theorem 11.4(i).

theorems.title: Norms in an unramified local extension
theorems.statement: If L/K is a finite unramified extension of nonarchimedean local fields, every unit of K is the norm of a unit of L. The valuation of a norm is a multiple of [L:K]. These two facts characterize the nonzero norms.
theorems.use: At an inert place of the unramified quadratic extension, even valuation therefore suffices. At a split place the norm sends (x,y) to xy, which attains every nonzero scalar.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, Chapter III, Proposition 1.2, with the norm of a uniformizer.

theorems.title: Lagrange inversion for formal power series
theorems.statement: Over a characteristic-zero field let T(u) have constant coefficient zero and invertible linear coefficient. Write u(T) for its inverse. For any power series H and n≥1, n[Tⁿ]H(u(T))=[uⁿ⁻¹]H′(u)(u/T(u))ⁿ.
theorems.use: Taking H to be the formal integral of the invariant differential gives λ₂₅=99/1280 on the curve at 5.
theorems.citation: I. M. Gessel, Lagrange Inversion, Theorem 2.1.1, formula (2.1.1).

theorems.title: The von Staudt–Clausen denominator theorem
theorems.statement: For even h≥2, adding 1/p to the Bernoulli number Bₕ for each prime p with p−1 dividing h gives an integer. Each such p occurs just once in the denominator.
theorems.use: For h≤k, all these primes are at most k+1. A single product of primes therefore clears the denominators in the character sum.
theorems.citation: K. Dilcher, NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §24.10(i), (24.10.1).

theorems.title: Fourier series of the Bernoulli polynomials
theorems.statement: For integer k≥2 and real x in [0,1], the Fourier coefficient of Bₖ at nonzero integer m is −k!/(2πim)ᵏ. The constant coefficient vanishes and the series converges absolutely.
theorems.use: Pairing the positive and negative frequencies bounds |Bₖ(x)| by 2k!ζ(k)/(2π)ᵏ at once for all x.
theorems.citation: K. Dilcher, NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, (24.8.3).

theorems.title: Euler’s evaluation of ζ(2)
theorems.statement: The series of reciprocal squares of the positive integers has sum π²/6.
theorems.use: For k≥2 the sum of reciprocal kth powers is at most ζ(2). Both signs of the frequencies in the Bernoulli series therefore cost at most π²/3<4.
theorems.citation: T. M. Apostol, NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, (25.6.1).

theorems.title: An elementary upper bound for the product of small primes
theorems.statement: For each integer N≥1 the product of the primes p≤N is at most 4ᴺ. For n≥2 the product over n<p≤2n divides the binomial coefficient (2n−1 choose n), which bounds the cost of doubling the cutoff.
theorems.use: At N=k+1 this bounds the size of the same integer that clears the Bernoulli denominators.
theorems.citation: A. Granville, The distribution of primes, Appendix E, Lemma E1.1 and Proposition E1.2.

theorems.title: Hensel lifting of a simple root
theorems.statement: For a complete discrete valuation ring R, a simple root of a monic polynomial modulo the maximal ideal lifts uniquely to a root in R with that residue.
theorems.use: At the inert prime p, the derivative 2δ is a unit. The two residue roots of X²+d lift distinctly, which identifies the sign of Frobenius on δ.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 10.153.9 and the simple-root criterion in §10.153.

theorems.title: Nakayama’s lemma
theorems.statement: If a finitely generated module M over a local ring with maximal ideal 𝔪 satisfies 𝔪M=M, then M is zero. In particular generators modulo 𝔪 lift to generators of M.
theorems.use: Apply this with 𝔪=(ℓ) to the finite-module quotient in the cokernel comparison. This gives the asserted bound for one additional cyclotomic layer.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 10.20.1, tag 00DV.

theorems.title: Minkowski’s bound for an ideal class
theorems.statement: For a number field of degree n and discriminant Δ with r₂ pairs of complex embeddings, every ideal class contains an integral ideal of norm at most (4/π)^(r₂)(n!/nⁿ)√|Δ|. Here the exponent r₂ counts conjugate pairs.
theorems.use: For ℚ(√−5) only norms one and two need checking. For ℚ(ζ₉) the bound is less than 4.47 and gives a second short list of ideals.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Theorem 4.3.

theorems.title: Minkowski’s convex body theorem
theorems.statement: Let Λ be a full lattice in ℝⁿ with covolume V. A convex body symmetric about the origin of volume greater than 2ⁿV contains a nonzero point of Λ.
theorems.use: The simultaneous bounds at the infinite places describe such a body in the real embedding space. Its volume grows with the denominator exponent, giving a nonzero field element small at every required embedding.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Theorem 4.19.

theorems.title: Shapiro’s lemma for group homology
theorems.statement: For a subgroup H of G and a left ℤH-module M, Hⱼ(G, ℤG⊗ℤH M) is naturally isomorphic to Hⱼ(H,M) in every degree j≥0. The tensor product here is over the group ring of H.
theorems.use: An orbit of chains gives an induced coefficient module. The lemma replaces its group homology by homology of the stabilizer, where the arithmetic estimates apply.
theorems.citation: C. A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Lemma 6.3.2.

theorems.title: The Ferrero–Washington theorem
theorems.statement: For every prime ℓ and abelian number field K, the cyclotomic ℤℓ-extension of K has Iwasawa μ-invariant zero.
theorems.use: The monograph needs a uniform upper bound on the number of generators of the ℓ-class groups of its finite layers. The tower argument reconstructs the class-group consequence used here.
theorems.citation: B. Ferrero and L. C. Washington, The Iwasawa invariant μₚ vanishes for abelian number fields, Annals of Mathematics 109 (1979), 377–395.

theorems.title: Weyl’s dimension formula
theorems.statement: For integral highest weight λ₁≥⋯≥λₙ, the dimension of the irreducible complex representation of U(n) is ∏_{i<j}(λᵢ−λⱼ+j−i)/(j−i). A common determinant twist leaves every difference unchanged.
theorems.use: At the real places the product of weight differences can be compared term by term with the Vandermonde factors in the formal degree.
theorems.citation: P. Etingof et al., Introduction to Representation Theory, §5.22, Theorem 5.22.1 and its dimension formula.

theorems.title: Schur–Weyl duality on tensor powers
theorems.statement: For a finite-dimensional complex vector space V, every endomorphism of V⊗ᵐ commuting with all g⊗ᵐ for g∈GL(V) is a linear combination of permutations of its m tensor factors.
theorems.use: The permutations give the trace contractions of the invariant tensors. Their cycles determine the powers acquired under block repetition.
theorems.citation: P. Etingof et al., Introduction to Representation Theory, §§5.18–5.19, the double centralizer and Schur–Weyl duality.

theorems.title: Hadamard’s determinant inequality
theorems.statement: The absolute determinant of a complex square matrix is at most the product of the Euclidean lengths of its columns. Applying this after taking a positive definite square root gives the corresponding Gram determinant bound.
theorems.use: Multiplying the local determinant bounds over the complex embeddings controls the ideal index of a set of short vectors.
theorems.citation: K. Lange, Hadamard’s Determinant Inequality, American Mathematical Monthly 121 (2014), 258–259.

theorems.title: Stokes’ theorem on a simplex
theorems.statement: On an oriented smooth p-simplex σ, the integral of a smooth (p−1)-form over the alternating boundary of σ equals the integral of its exterior derivative over σ.
theorems.use: A closed form thus vanishes on boundaries when integrated over chains. Its period depends only on the homology class.
theorems.citation: D. Calegari, Notes on Differential Forms, Theorem 2.1.

theorems.title: Cauchy’s theorem for a finite group
theorems.statement: For a prime ℓ dividing the order of a finite group, the group has an element of order ℓ.
theorems.use: The exponent bound on the Galois quotient then forces every odd prime dividing its order to divide the fixed level order.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Group Theory, Theorem 4.13.

theorems.title: Howe duality for local unitary pairs
theorems.statement: Over a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic different from two, the small theta lift of an irreducible smooth representation for a unitary dual pair is either zero or irreducible. Distinct representations with nonzero lifts have distinct partners.
theorems.use: This gives the local uniqueness underlying the pairing condition. The row argument separately uses its global pairing hypothesis, positivity of the Gram operator and spanning of the target by orthogonal components.
theorems.citation: W. T. Gan and S. Takeda, A proof of the Howe duality conjecture, Theorem 1.2.

theorems.title: Sinnott’s separation principle
theorems.statement: Suppose Y₁,…,Yₘ are pairwise multiplicatively independent nontrivial Laurent monomials in independent variables over a field k. If ∑rⱼ(Yⱼ)=0 for rational functions rⱼ over k, every rⱼ is constant.
theorems.use: This is the independence principle behind the separation argument. The finite group-algebra proof in the chapter supplies the required congruence depth and isolates an individual coefficient.
theorems.citation: W. Sinnott, On a theorem of L. Washington, Astérisque 147–148 (1987), appendix restating Proposition 3.1 of his 1984 paper.

theorems.title: Siegel’s lower bound on a real exceptional zero
theorems.statement: For every ε>0 there is c(ε)>0 such that a real zero β of a real nonprincipal Dirichlet character of modulus m satisfies 1−β≥c(ε)m⁻ᵋ. The constant is ineffective.
theorems.use: The progression estimate needs a positive lower bound for the distance of the possible exceptional zero from one. Taking ε=1 gives the coarser scale c/m.
theorems.citation: D. Koukoulopoulos, The Distribution of Prime Numbers, Theorem 12.10.

theorems.title: Perron inversion for the ramp
theorems.statement: For c>1 and t>0, the inverse Mellin integral of tˢ/[s(s−1)] along Re s=c, with measure ds/(2πi), is max(t−1,0). The two simple poles at 1 and 0 give the term t−1 for t>1.
theorems.use: On a line where the Dirichlet series converges absolutely, take t=u/n and sum with coefficients Λ(n)χ(n). This gives the contour representation used to compare two endpoints.
theorems.citation: D. Koukoulopoulos, The Distribution of Prime Numbers, Chapters 5 and 7 on Perron inversion. The stated ramp kernel follows by integrating the step kernel.

theorems.title: Digamma values at one and one half
theorems.statement: For ψ=Γ′/Γ, one has ψ(1)=−γ and ψ(1/2)=−γ−2 log 2, where γ is Euler’s constant.
theorems.use: The logarithmic derivative of the completed odd quadratic L-function contains these two values when reflected between zero and one. Their mean determines the constant in the CM period identity.
theorems.citation: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §5.4(ii), (5.4.12) and (5.4.13).

theorems.title: The geometric series and its tail
theorems.statement: If 0 ≤ q < 1 and H is a nonnegative integer, the sum of qʰ for h ≥ H is qᴴ/(1−q). Multiplication of a finite sum by 1−q cancels consecutive terms, and the remaining endpoint tends to zero.
theorems.use: The count at one complex place grows by at most a square of the radius for each minor. The cubic weight leaves a decaying geometric series in each place index.
theorems.citation: Gilbert Strang, Calculus, §10.1, equations (1)–(2).

theorems.title: An orthonormal eigenbasis for the Gram operator
theorems.statement: On a finite-dimensional complex inner product space every self-adjoint operator has an orthonormal eigenbasis. The eigenvalues of A*A are nonnegative because its quadratic form is the squared norm of Ax. Its zero eigenspace is the kernel of A.
theorems.use: The positive eigenvalues count image dimensions and their first and second power sums give the two traces in the rank estimate. In the unitary period the same diagonalization describes principal determinants and the polar factor. In the cohomological integral it gives a bounded frame and identifies the real Jacobian.
theorems.citation: Sheldon Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right, 4th edition, §7B, theorem 7.31, and §7C on positive operators.

theorems.title: Cauchy–Schwarz for the nonzero eigenvalues
theorems.statement: For k real numbers λᵢ, (Σ λᵢ)² ≤ k Σ λᵢ². This follows by taking the inner product of the vector of entries with the vector of k ones.
theorems.use: When the entries are the positive eigenvalues of the frame operator, the quotient of the squared trace by the trace of its square is a lower bound for its rank. In the unitary period, at most twice the real rank many eigenvalues enter each partial sum.
theorems.citation: Sheldon Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right, 4th edition, §6A, inequality 6.14 and example 6.16(a).

theorems.title: The field norm as a product of conjugates
theorems.statement: In a number field E the determinant of multiplication by x is the product of τ(x) over the embeddings into ℂ. If x is a nonzero algebraic integer, this determinant is a nonzero rational integer. In a CM field the complex embeddings pair up, giving the squared absolute value at each pair.
theorems.use: Apply the norm to the difference of two distinct integral minors. Their images cannot occupy the same half-unit cell at every complex place.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Chapter 2, Proposition 2.19 and its proof.

theorems.title: Rank and nullity
theorems.statement: For a linear map on a finite-dimensional domain, the dimension of the kernel plus the dimension of the image equals the domain dimension. Extend a basis of the kernel to one of the whole domain. The images of the added basis vectors form a basis of the image.
theorems.use: An upper bound for the dimension lost to the kernel gives the number of independent images of one word.
theorems.citation: Sheldon Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right, 4th edition, §3B, theorem 3.21.

theorems.title: Cycling rectangular factors under the trace
theorems.statement: If A has m rows and n columns and B has n rows and m columns, then tr(AB) = tr(BA). Both traces sum the same products of matrix entries over all row and column indices.
theorems.use: Moving the period matrix past its adjoint turns the two traces on the common row space into sums of squared inner products between columns.
theorems.citation: Sheldon Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right, 4th edition, §8D, theorem 8.49.

theorems.title: Stickelberger annihilation in a cyclotomic field
theorems.statement: Let L = ℚ(ζₘ), G = Gal(L/ℚ), and Θ = (1/m) Σₜ [t]ₘ σₜ⁻¹, summing over unit classes and using their least nonnegative representatives. For β in ℤ[G] such that βΘ has integral coefficients, βΘ acts as zero on the ideal class group of L.
theorems.use: An explicit β gives the integral relation on the image of 1−J, including when ℓ is two. The text reconstructs the relation by carries and Jacobi sums.
theorems.citation: C. S. Yogananda, “Stickelberger Revisited”, p. 151, opening theorem, in Cyclotomic Fields and Related Topics.

theorems.title: Abel’s partial summation formula
theorems.statement: Let A(t) be the sum of aₙ over positive integers n ≤ t and let f be continuously differentiable on [y,z]. Then the sum of aₙ f(n) over y < n ≤ z equals A(z)f(z) − A(y)f(y) − ∫ᵧᶻ A(t)f′(t) dt.
theorems.use: Weighting the logarithmic prime sum by the reciprocal logarithm transfers its error to a bound for counting primes in a residue class.
theorems.citation: Dimitris Koukoulopoulos, The Distribution of Prime Numbers, §1, formula (1.8) and Example 1.8.

theorems.title: Euclidean transference for the covering radius
theorems.statement: For a full lattice of positive dimension D in a Euclidean space, the covering radius times the length of the shortest nonzero vector in the Euclidean dual lattice is at most D/2.
theorems.use: A lower bound on a trace-dual matrix gives an integral matrix close to any family of real-place targets after accounting for the factor two in the field trace.
theorems.citation: W. Banaszczyk, “New bounds in some transference theorems in the geometry of numbers”, Mathematische Annalen 296 (1993), 625–635.

theorems.title: A finite torsion-free module over a Dedekind domain is projective
theorems.statement: Over a Dedekind domain, every finitely generated torsion-free module is finite locally free and hence projective. A surjection onto such a module has a linear section.
theorems.use: Splitting off the quotient by the orthogonal sublattice provides the integral projection used to lift a rounded matrix on the middle layer.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 15.22.11(2) and the finite projective criteria of Lemma 10.78.2.

theorems.title: The norm of the different ideal
theorems.statement: For a number field E the inverse different consists of the elements pairing integrally with the ring of integers under the field trace. Its inverse ideal, the different, has absolute norm |disc(E)|.
theorems.use: Multiplication by the different clears the denominator of a trace-dual map. Its effect on a normalized lattice size is the root discriminant.
theorems.citation: Keith Conrad, The Different Ideal, §4, in particular Theorem 4.8.

theorems.title: Turán’s second main theorem on power sums
theorems.statement: If n ≥ 1 complex numbers are ordered by decreasing modulus with the largest modulus one, then for every integer h ≥ 0 one of the next n powers has a sum of modulus at least 2[n/(8e(h+n))]ⁿ when all coefficients are one.
theorems.use: The minimum of the initial coefficient sums is one. Weakening 8e to 1600 gives the bound used to detect the distinguished zero among the other zero distances.
theorems.citation: H. L. Montgomery and R. C. Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory III, Appendix K, §K.2, Theorem K.3, p. 350.

theorems.title: The lowest compact type of a discrete series
theorems.statement: For U(p,q) with a regular Harish-Chandra parameter λ and a compatible choice of positive roots, the lowest compact type has highest weight λ plus the half-sum of the positive noncompact roots minus the half-sum of the positive compact roots. Its multiplicity is one.
theorems.use: This identifies the compact type at derivative order zero. The other reachable types are controlled by roots acting on this space.
theorems.citation: D. Vogan, Understanding restriction to K, slide 8, theorem of Schmid and Hecht–Schmid. For U(p,q) the formula is also (2.24) of Harris, Kobayashi and Speh.

theorems.title: The scalar of the quadratic matrix Casimir
theorems.statement: For the trace pairing on gl(n), the sum of EᵢⱼEⱼᵢ acts by ∥λ∥² − ∥ρ∥² at infinitesimal character λ, where ρ is the half sum of positive roots. On a highest-weight module of highest weight μ, λ = μ + ρ.
theorems.use: Apply the same identity to the two compact blocks and subtract the full Casimir to compute the sum of squared derivative norms.
theorems.citation: Zhuoke Yang, New approaches to the gl(N) weight system, Izvestiya Mathematics 87 (2023), §5, Example 5.4, p. 1265.

theorems.title: Witt’s extension theorem for a Hermitian space
theorems.statement: Over a field, a linear isometry between two subspaces of a finite-dimensional nondegenerate Hermitian space extends to an isometry of the whole space.
theorems.use: Apply extension to the lines generated by two vectors of the same nonzero length. A direct basis argument covers the split quadratic algebra.
theorems.citation: D. Sprehn and N. Wahl, Forms over fields and Witt’s lemma, Theorem 3.4.

theorems.title: A locally bounded measurable section of a homogeneous space
theorems.statement: For a second-countable locally compact group G and closed subgroup H, the map G → G/H has a Borel section taking compact sets into relatively compact sets.
theorems.use: Select an isometry for each first vector measurably. On a compact family of first vectors the choices stay in a compact part of the group after taking closure.
theorems.citation: E. T. Kehlet, Cross sections for quotient maps of locally compact groups. See D. P. Williams, Crossed Products of C*-Algebras, Theorem 4.33 and the preceding note on second countability.

theorems.title: The trace pairing of a separable field extension
theorems.statement: For a finite separable extension L/K, the bilinear pairing (a,b) ↦ Tr(ab) is nondegenerate.
theorems.use: A nonsingular Hermitian space over a quadratic finite-field extension has a vector of nonzero Hermitian value, including in residue characteristic two.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Fields, Lemma 9.20.7.

theorems.title: Weak approximation at finitely many places
theorems.statement: For a field with finitely many pairwise inequivalent nontrivial absolute values, the diagonal field is dense in the product of its completions.
theorems.use: Approximate the entries of a skew-adjoint matrix at the one or two primes over a finite base place. Continuity of the Cayley transform then yields a rational isometry in the desired open coset.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Theorem 7.20 and its consequence for completions.

theorems.title: Lebesgue’s dominated convergence theorem
theorems.statement: If measurable functions converge almost everywhere and their absolute values are bounded by a common integrable function, the integrals converge to the integral of the limit.
theorems.use: An integrable inverse power of the radius on one regular Gram fibre controls the translates of a Schwartz test on nearby fibres.
theorems.citation: Sheldon Axler, Measure, Integration & Real Analysis, Theorem 3.31.

theorems.title: The analytic class number formula
theorems.statement: For a totally complex field of degree 2f the Dedekind zeta function has residue (2π)ᶠhR/(w√|disc E|) at one, where h is the class number, R the regulator in the doubled complex logarithms, and w the number of roots of unity.
theorems.use: The archimedean mass of all rank-one coefficient classes gives the initial value in the induction on block rank.
theorems.citation: A. V. Sutherland, Number Theory I (Fall 2021), Lecture 19, Theorem 19.12.

theorems.title: Poisson summation on a Euclidean lattice
theorems.statement: For a full lattice L and a Schwartz function f, the sum of f over L is the sum of its Fourier transform over the dual lattice divided by the covolume of L, with Fourier kernel exp(−2πi⟨x,y⟩). The Gaussian exp(−π‖x‖²) is its own Fourier transform.
theorems.use: The zero vector on each side supplies the unmarked term when integrating the Gaussian identity across the space of coefficient lattices.
theorems.citation: O. Regev, Lattices in Computer Science, Fourier Transform, Poisson Summation Formula and Example 5.

theorems.title: Finite volume of the adelic quotient
theorems.statement: For a connected linear algebraic group over a number field, the quotient of its adelic group by its rational points has finite invariant volume if it has no nontrivial rational character defined over the base field.
theorems.use: The determinant changes to its inverse under the quadratic involution. The resulting unitary group has no nontrivial base-field character, so the transverse isometry group contributes finite volume.
theorems.citation: A. Borel, Some finiteness properties of adele groups over number fields, Publ. Math. IHÉS 16 (1963), Theorem 5.6(i), p. 21.

theorems.title: Compactness of the norm-one idèle classes
theorems.statement: The idèles of modulus one in a number field, modulo the embedded nonzero field elements, form a compact topological group.
theorems.use: After removing the common real height, finitely many relatively compact sets lift a cover of this quotient. They control the multiplicative coordinate in each logarithmic shell.
theorems.citation: A. Borel, Some finiteness properties of adele groups over number fields, Publ. Math. IHÉS 16 (1963), Theorem 5.8, special case following the theorem, p. 22.

theorems.title: Baire category for a locally compact orbit
theorems.statement: If a nonempty locally compact Hausdorff space is a countable union of closed subsets, some member has nonempty interior.
theorems.use: A countable family of translates covers the closed orbit. One has interior, which gives a neighbourhood in the image of a prescribed neighbourhood of the identity under the orbit map.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Topology, Lemma 5.13.3, tag 0CQN.

theorems.title: When an adèle is invertible
theorems.statement: An adèle of a number field is a unit precisely when every component is nonzero and its valuation is zero at almost every finite place.
theorems.use: The inverse norm of a selected column denominator has integral components away from a finite set. This allows division simultaneously over the adelic coefficient algebra.
theorems.citation: Andrew V. Sutherland, 18.785 Number Theory I, Fall 2019, Lecture 26, Definition 26.2 and its derivation.

theorems.title: Uniqueness of the primitive inducing character
theorems.statement: Every Dirichlet character comes from a unique primitive character of conductor dividing its modulus. Two primitive characters inducing the same character at a common multiple therefore coincide, including their conductors.
theorems.use: For distinct primitive characters, the product of one with the conjugate of the other is nonprincipal after passage to a common modulus. Its sum over a complete period vanishes.
theorems.citation: Andrew V. Sutherland, 18.785 Number Theory I, Fall 2021, Theorem 18.13 and Corollary 18.15.

theorems.title: The radial gamma integral and sphere area
theorems.statement: For real a and b positive, the integral of exp(−rᵃ) rᵇ⁻¹ over the positive reals equals Γ(b/a)/a. At positive integers Γ(m+1) equals m!.
theorems.use: Equating radial and Cartesian evaluations of the complex Gaussian integral gives the sphere factors left after taking the quotient of compact volumes.
theorems.citation: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, equations 5.9.1 and 5.4.1.

theorems.title: Nonvanishing on the line of real part one away from its real point
theorems.statement: For a Dirichlet character χ and any nonzero real t, L(1+it,χ) is nonzero.
theorems.use: Together with nonvanishing at one for a nonprincipal character and the absolutely convergent Euler product to the right, this places the selected zeros strictly to the left of one.
theorems.citation: K. S. Kedlaya, Notes on analytic number theory, Theorem 3.8.

theorems.title: Strict separation of disjoint compact convex sets
theorems.statement: Two nonempty disjoint compact convex sets in a finite-dimensional real vector space lie in opposite open half-spaces of an affine hyperplane.
theorems.use: The two sets contain the witnesses of an incompatible label and a maximal face. Cutting between them decreases the finite number of realized faces on both sides and on their section.
theorems.citation: S. Boyd and L. Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, §2.5.1, pp. 46–47, shortest-segment proof.

theorems.title: Uniqueness of Haar measure up to a positive constant
theorems.statement: On a locally compact Hausdorff group two nonzero left Haar measures differ by a positive scalar. Transport by a topological group isomorphism gives another Haar measure.
theorems.use: At one real place and then on the product, a scalar compares two normalizations. It multiplies the coefficient integral and the diagonal quantity used to normalize it.
theorems.citation: A. V. Sutherland, Number Theory I, Fall 2016, Lecture 13, Theorem 13.3.

theorems.title: The determinant after replacing a column
theorems.statement: If c is a column vector, replacing column j of a square matrix G by Gc gives determinant cⱼ det G. This follows by multilinearity and also holds for singular matrices.
theorems.use: Replacing one column relates a single coordinate of a vector to a determinant with bounded entries. This is the step that turns a bound for the whole form into a bound for every coordinate.
theorems.citation: G. Strang, MIT 18.06, Spring 2010, Lecture 20, Cramer’s rule, inverse matrix, and volume. The column identity is proved in the linked passage.

theorems.title: The long exact homology sequence
theorems.statement: A short exact sequence of chain complexes gives a long exact sequence of homology groups. Its connecting map takes a cycle in the quotient, lifts it to the middle complex, and takes the class of the lifted boundary in the subcomplex.
theorems.use: For a permutation module mapping onto the coefficient module this compares torsion in the target homology with the finite homology of the permutation module and torsion one degree lower in the kernel.
theorems.citation: C. A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Theorem 1.3.1, p. 10.

theorems.title: Schur orthogonality for a square-integrable unitary representation
theorems.statement: For an irreducible square-integrable unitary representation of a unimodular group with fixed Haar measure, the integral of |⟨u,π(g)v⟩|² is ‖u‖²‖v‖²/dπ. Polarization gives orthogonality for mixed coefficients. The positive constant dπ is its formal degree for this measure.
theorems.use: The total mass of the mixed coefficient and its mass on each stabilizer fibre refer to two distinct formal degrees. Orthogonality also turns the entries of the period operator into coefficients of an orthogonal family in L².
theorems.citation: M. Duflo and C. C. Moore, On the regular representation of a nonunimodular locally compact group, J. Funct. Anal. 21 (1976), 209–243, specialized to a unimodular group.

theorems.title: Spectral theorem for a compact self-adjoint operator
theorems.statement: For a compact self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space the closed span of its nonzero eigenspaces is the orthogonal complement of its kernel. Each nonzero eigenspace has finite dimension. The quadratic form is the sum of the eigenvalues weighted by the squared coordinates in an orthonormal eigenbasis.
theorems.use: A positive lower bound on the quadratic form at the projected vector forces a positive eigenvalue of the required size.
theorems.citation: MIT 18.102, Introduction to Functional Analysis, Lecture 22, Theorem 232.

theorems.title: A linear change of variables in real volume
theorems.statement: On a finite-dimensional real vector space an invertible linear map A multiplies Lebesgue measure by |det A|. In an integral of f(Ax) with respect to the original variable x, substitution on the image therefore introduces the reciprocal factor.
theorems.use: On the product of Hermitian matrix spaces the reciprocal Jacobian compares integrals on a compact set and its image.
theorems.citation: J. Hunter, Measure Theory, §2.8, Linear transformations.

theorems.title: Volume under a linear automorphism over a local field
theorems.statement: On an additive vector space over a nonarchimedean local field, applying an invertible matrix to a measurable set multiplies its Haar volume by the normalized absolute value of the determinant. The pushforward measure of a fixed set gains the reciprocal factor.
theorems.use: On each horizontal coordinate, multiplication by the conjugate scalar has determinant equal to the quadratic norm. That norm also acts on one central coordinate.
theorems.citation: H. Glöckner, Lectures on Lie groups over local fields, Lemma 1.5, p. 8.

theorems.title: Finite real covolume of an arithmetic subgroup
theorems.statement: Let G be a connected linear algebraic group over the rationals with trivial rational character group. An arithmetic subgroup of G has finite covolume in its real points for Haar measure.
theorems.use: For each finite adelic lattice class, restriction of scalars expresses its archimedean stabilizer as an arithmetic subgroup. The conjugation of a unitary determinant rules out nontrivial rational characters.
theorems.citation: A. Borel and Harish-Chandra, Arithmetic Subgroups of Algebraic Groups, Theorem 9.4, Annals of Mathematics 75 (1962), p. 522.

theorems.title: Complete reducibility for a compact group
theorems.statement: A finite-dimensional continuous complex representation of a compact Lie group splits as a sum of irreducibles. Averaging a positive Hermitian form gives an invariant inner product, so the orthogonal complement of an invariant subspace is invariant.
theorems.use: The array carrying the derivative in one direction splits into compact types. On each type the Casimir acts by a scalar, which can then be summed over the orthogonal components.
theorems.citation: P. Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Corollary 35.2.

theorems.title: The product formula for a discrete-series formal degree
theorems.statement: For a regular Harish-Chandra parameter on U(p,q), with its Haar measure fixed, the formal degree is a common positive constant times the product of the pairwise parameter gaps in absolute value divided by the corresponding Weyl denominators.
theorems.use: A shift of one coordinate changes only the factors touching that coordinate. Comparing with the same Haar measure cancels the common constant and gives the reciprocal-degree bound in the tensor moment.
theorems.citation: M. F. Atiyah and W. Schmid, A geometric construction of the discrete series for semisimple Lie groups, §5, p. 25, after (5.15).

theorems.title: Cayley–Hamilton
theorems.statement: A square matrix over a commutative ring satisfies its own monic characteristic polynomial.
theorems.use: After the power traces force the characteristic polynomial to be (T−1)ⁿ, evaluating at the rational matrix proves that subtracting the identity gives a nilpotent matrix.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 10.16.1, Tag 00DX.

theorems.title: Mass formula for a maximal definite Hermitian lattice
theorems.statement: For a totally definite Hermitian space over a quadratic extension of a totally real number field, the mass of the genus of a maximal lattice has a product formula. In the finite-unramified case used here the constant common to spaces of fixed rank is the mass of the orthonormal genus. A finite set of nonunimodular local factors accounts for the other maximal genera.
theorems.use: The local factors at the bad places bound the mass of maximal enlargements. Counting smaller lattices inside these enlargements then gives the bound at an arbitrary discriminant order.
theorems.citation: W. T. Gan, J. P. Hanke and J.-K. Yu, On an exact mass formula of Shimura, Propositions 4.4 and 4.5, p. 110 (odd and even unitary ranks).

theorems.title: Factorization, norm and degrees of prime ideals
theorems.statement: Every nonzero proper integral ideal in a number ring factors uniquely into prime ideals. The absolute norm is multiplicative. For a rational prime p the sum of the products of ramification index and residue degree over the primes above p equals the field degree D. The prime of residue degree f has absolute norm pᶠ.
theorems.use: Factoring off one prime above a chosen divisor of the norm gives at most D choices. Iterating bounds the number of possible bad ideals and hence the number of rational orbit representatives.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, §§3–4, particularly Theorem 3.34 and the definition of the ideal norm.

theorems.title: The quantum comatrix identity
theorems.statement: For the matrix of elementary generators of gl(m) the ordered column determinant with consecutive unit shifts admits a cofactor expansion. The signed comatrix on the left times the shifted generating matrix on the right is the diagonal matrix of that determinant.
theorems.use: Alternating the columns and expanding the last one gives an operator identity on smooth vectors. Specialization at a simple root then recovers the required tensor projection.
theorems.citation: A. I. Molev, Yangians and their applications, Definition 2.26 and Proposition 2.27, formulas (2.30)–(2.31), under the evaluation representation.

theorems.title: The central character of the Capelli determinant
theorems.statement: For gl(m) with column parameters u, u−1, …, u−m+1, the full Capelli determinant has central coefficients. At highest weight μ, with coordinates numbered from zero, its scalar is the product of u+μⱼ−j.
theorems.use: Converting the highest weight to the infinitesimal character gives the m distinct factors in the projector calculation.
theorems.citation: A. I. Molev, Sugawara Operators for Classical Lie Algebras, §4.6, formula (4.37) and Corollary 4.6.2.

theorems.title: Signed interlacing for a discrete-series summand
theorems.statement: For the restriction from U(p,q) to U(p−1,q), a discrete series of the smaller group occurs discretely precisely when the two signed Harish-Chandra parameters satisfy the signed interlacing law. In the merged decreasing lists, consecutive entries from the same group have opposite signs and consecutive entries from different groups have the same sign, with signs interpreted for the positive line removed here.
theorems.use: This branching criterion identifies the occurrence required by the period. The chapter explains the propagation of a known occurrence through a lowering of an ambient parameter and the recovery of an intertwiner from a nonzero coefficient.
theorems.citation: Hongyu He, On the Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for U(p,q), Definition 1 and Theorem 0.1, with the positive-line convention.

theorems.title: Index of a rank-one ideal sublattice
theorems.statement: For a number ring R, a nonzero fractional ideal J and a nonzero integral ideal 𝔞, the additive index [J:𝔞J] equals the absolute norm of 𝔞. Every full sublattice ideal I contained in J is uniquely 𝔞J with 𝔞=IJ⁻¹.
theorems.use: The discriminant of a line sublattice grows by the square of this index, so counting ideals up to a norm cutoff counts all eligible sublattices in each maximal line lattice.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Theorem 3.32 and Proposition 4.2 on ideal norms and indices.

theorems.title: Brauer–Nesbitt in characteristic zero
theorems.statement: Two finite-dimensional semisimple representations of a group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero are isomorphic if their characteristic polynomials coincide at every group element.
theorems.use: Apply the assertion after adding the opposite character list to each odd-dimensional companion. The chapter proves it by simultaneous density on the simple constituents.
theorems.citation: P. Etingof et al., Introduction to Representation Theory, Theorem 2.5(ii) and Theorem 2.17(i).

theorems.title: Density of the compact-finite vectors
theorems.statement: In a continuous unitary representation of a compact Lie group, the Hilbert space is the closure of the sum of its finite-dimensional irreducible subrepresentations. The character projections onto compact types preserve smooth ambient vectors under a smooth ambient group action.
theorems.use: Applied to a smooth ambient trial vector, compact approximation and the Casimir estimate together control the error of every smaller-block derivative.
theorems.citation: P. Etingof, Representations of Lie Groups, Lecture 4, Corollary 4.7.

theorems.title: Potential semistability of a de Rham representation
theorems.statement: Over a finite extension of ℚℓ, a finite-dimensional de Rham Galois representation with finite ℓ-adic coefficient field becomes semistable after a finite extension.
theorems.use: For the residual de Rham constituent the attached Weil–Deligne representation can be compared with the corresponding summand of the odd-rank representation.
theorems.citation: L. Berger, Représentations p-adiques et équations différentielles, Inventiones Mathematicae 148 (2002), 219–284.

theorems.title: Continuous functional calculus for a bounded self-adjoint operator
theorems.statement: Real continuous functions on a closed interval containing the spectrum act by self-adjoint operators, compatibly with sums, products and uniform limits. A nonnegative function gives a positive operator.
theorems.use: The positive and negative parts of the bounded inverse shifted by one half have zero product and commute with the group.
theorems.citation: R. Melrose, Functional Analysis, Chapter 3, Theorem 3.5 and Remark 3.1.

theorems.title: Orthogonal projection onto a closed subspace
theorems.statement: Each vector of a Hilbert space has a unique decomposition into one vector in a given closed linear subspace and another in its perpendicular.
theorems.use: Projection onto the closure of the range of the smooth quadratic operator proves that its range is dense.
theorems.citation: R. Melrose, Functional Analysis, Chapter 3, §9, Proposition 3.6.

theorems.title: Local factors of an irreducible admissible automorphic representation
theorems.statement: An irreducible admissible smooth module for the finite-adelic Hecke algebra factors as a restricted tensor product of irreducible admissible local modules.
theorems.use: At a split place the local factor is a representation of a general linear group. A vector fixed by its integral subgroup detects a spherical summand.
theorems.citation: D. Flath, Decomposition of representations into tensor products, Theorem 2 (p. 181). See also J. R. Getz, An introduction to automorphic representations, Theorem 7.5.

theorems.title: Satake parameters for a spherical representation
theorems.statement: For an irreducible spherical representation of GLₙ over a nonarchimedean local field, the spherical Hecke character determines an unordered n-tuple of nonzero complex numbers in the chosen Satake normalization.
theorems.use: This tuple supplies the source polynomial at a good split place before the two lists of auxiliary characters are added.
theorems.citation: I. Satake, Theory of spherical functions on reductive algebraic groups over p-adic fields, Theorems 2 and 3.

theorems.title: The square of the Dirac operator on a compact type
theorems.statement: The square of the Dirac operator relates the full Casimir and the compact Casimir on the tensor with the exterior module. The chapter gives the scalar and the exterior correction for its chosen convention.
theorems.use: The two halves vanish on a selected compact highest vector. The square then fixes the full Casimir eigenvalue on the terminal type.
theorems.citation: R. Parthasarathy, Dirac operator and the discrete series, Proposition 3.1 and its specialization in Proposition 3.2.

theorems.title: The semisimple quotient of a pseudocharacter
theorems.statement: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the quotient of the group algebra by the trace radical of a finite-degree pseudocharacter is a finite product of full matrix algebras. The trace on each surviving block is an integer multiple of its ordinary trace.
theorems.use: This algebra realizes the limiting trace as a semisimple representation of the required rank. Its nondegenerate trace pairing also recovers matrix entries continuously.
theorems.citation: R. Rouquier, Caractérisation des caractères et pseudo-caractères, Journal of Algebra 180 (1996), Lemma 4.1 and §4.

theorems.title: Taylor’s formula with Lagrange remainder
theorems.statement: For a real function with m continuous derivatives on the closed interval between t and t+δ, the difference from its degree-(m−1) Taylor polynomial at t is bounded by |δ|ᵐ/m! times the supremum of its mth derivative in absolute value on that interval.
theorems.use: Pairing a Hilbert-space Taylor remainder with its own unit direction yields the norm estimate for a noncompact group translate.
theorems.citation: MIT 18.014, Calculus with Theory, Chapter O, Theorem 2.

theorems.title: Finiteness and cohomological dimension of geometric étale cohomology
theorems.statement: For a smooth projective variety of dimension n over a number field and a prime ℓ, geometric étale cohomology with ℚℓ coefficients is finite-dimensional and vanishes in degrees greater than 2n. The natural absolute Galois action is continuous.
theorems.use: The simultaneous Hecke eigenspace is taken inside a finite sum with a continuous Galois action.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Lectures on Étale Cohomology, Theorems 15.1 and 19.2. For continuity see Brinon–Conrad, Example 1.2.3, linked in the passage.

theorems.title: Crystalline summands and filtered de Rham periods
theorems.statement: A Galois-stable direct summand of a crystalline representation is crystalline. Its filtered de Rham periods form a filtered direct summand, and the dimensions of each graded piece add across a direct sum.
theorems.use: Two split injections in opposite directions transfer crystallinity to the rank-m model and force all the specified filtration jumps to occur.
theorems.citation: O. Brinon and B. Conrad, CMI Summer School Notes on p-adic Hodge Theory, Theorem 5.2.1 and §6.3.

theorems.title: The holomorphic Lefschetz formula at transverse fixed points
theorems.statement: For a holomorphic self-map of a compact complex manifold with isolated nondegenerate fixed points, the alternating trace on cohomology of holomorphic a-forms is the sum at the fixed points of the trace on the ath exterior power of the cotangent pullback divided by det(I−A), where A is the derivative.
theorems.use: The elliptic-curve example evaluates the two holomorphic degrees. The general geometric input for two correspondence maps is stated in the book.
theorems.citation: M. F. Atiyah and R. Bott, A Lefschetz fixed point formula for elliptic complexes II, Annals of Mathematics 88 (1968), 451–491, holomorphic case.

theorems.title: Extension of an embedding inside a Galois extension
theorems.statement: If Ω/F is Galois and F⊆L⊆Ω, any F-embedding of L into Ω extends to an F-automorphism of Ω.
theorems.use: An embedding of a field generated by finitely many Hecke coordinates determines one of the finitely many simultaneous conjugates of the whole system.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Fields and Galois Theory, Proposition 7.4.

theorems.title: Completeness of a finite-dimensional normed space over a complete field
theorems.statement: On a finite-dimensional vector space over a complete valued field every vector-space norm induces the same complete topology.
theorems.use: The field generated by the original rational Hecke coordinates has bounded finite degree and is complete, so the trace-limit averages converge in this field.
theorems.citation: A. Sutherland, MIT 18.785, Fall 2016, Lecture 10, Proposition 10.6.

theorems.title: Vanishing of nonzero cyclotomic twisted invariants
theorems.statement: Over a finite extension of ℚℓ, the completed algebraic closure has no nonzero element on which the absolute Galois group acts by a nonzero integral power of the cyclotomic character.
theorems.use: A Galois-stable relation with minimal monomial support lies in a single column weight.
theorems.citation: O. Brinon and B. Conrad, CMI Summer School Notes on p-adic Hodge Theory, Theorem 2.2.7.

theorems.title: From de Rham jumps to the Hodge–Tate decomposition
theorems.statement: For a de Rham representation, the associated graded space of its filtered de Rham periods identifies with its graded Hodge–Tate periods. A jump of degree h corresponds to a completed coefficient line with cyclotomic twist −h.
theorems.use: The multiplicities of the inducing embedding give the columns of the local comparison and the signs of the cocharacter exponents.
theorems.citation: O. Brinon and B. Conrad, CMI Summer School Notes on p-adic Hodge Theory, Example 6.3.1 and Proposition 6.3.2.

theorems.title: Hilbert’s Nullstellensatz for a maximal ideal
theorems.statement: A maximal ideal of a nonzero finitely generated algebra over an algebraically closed field has that field as its residue field.
theorems.use: Inverting the product of finitely many tests before taking a residue field preserves all of the required inequalities.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Theorem 10.34.1 (tag 00FV).

theorems.title: The radical of a finite-dimensional algebra
theorems.statement: The ideal annihilating every simple module is the largest nilpotent two-sided ideal of the algebra.
theorems.use: Its image on the original representation has a stable complement and must vanish.
theorems.citation: P. Etingof et al., Introduction to representation theory, Lemma 2.8 and Proposition 2.11.

theorems.title: Elimination in an invertible matrix
theorems.statement: Over a field an invertible matrix can be reduced to a nonsingular diagonal matrix by adding multiples of other rows.
theorems.use: Each row addition lifts to a transvection in the tangent-generated matrix algebra.
theorems.citation: MIT 18.700, Gaussian elimination, Theorem 4.8, with the row-addition pivot argument in the text.

theorems.title: Finiteness of the adelic class number
theorems.statement: For the connected unitary group over the number field, the rational points have finitely many classes modulo the archimedean group and the standard integral finite level. The same holds at each compact open finite level.
theorems.use: A single bound over finitely many representatives controls every integral evaluation of an algebraic form.
theorems.citation: A. Borel, Some finiteness properties of adele groups over number fields, Theorem 5.1.
